analysis.title: Retail Radar: Nov 11 – Early Sellers, Quickly Back in the Market
key_insights: Last Thursday (Nov 5) the Nasdaq fell 6.4%, its largest decline since March 2020, and the S&P 500 fell 4.4%, with AI upstream names at the epicenter. Retail was a record seller of cash equities early in the session (-6z at 10am).

Single-stock selling in the first 30 minutes was the strongest in over 5 years (-6.2z), and ETF selling was -2.3z. Tech was ~75% of single-stock liquidations (Tech ex-Mag 7 -6.2z, Mag 7 -3.9z). About 80% of the day's dollar selling was done in the first half hour, and selling paused after 11am.

JPM says it cannot rule out that retail drove Thursday's decline, though it is hard to quantify. Other participants amplified it: CTAs turned net short US equities, vol-targeting funds' target leverage fell from the ~65th to the 30th percentile, and dealer long-gamma support fell to the 12th percentile.

Retail bought the rebound on Friday (~49th percentile) and Monday (~70th percentile), bought the CPI-led weakness on Tuesday (~68th percentile) after a stronger-than-expected CPI print, and faded on Wednesday (58th percentile at 11am, 8th percentile at 4pm).

Despite Thursday's liquidation, retail was a net buyer of Tech for the week (stocks +0.2z, ETFs +0.1z). Buying was entirely Mag 7 (+1.1z) while Tech ex-Mag 7 saw net selling (-1.1z). Retail bought Semis and sold Hardware and Software.

NVDA was retail's favorite: +2.8z over the week, with dip buying of +3.7z Monday and +4.7z Tuesday after a ~10% decline. It is also the most retail-bought stock year to date, followed by MSFT and TSLA.

Weekly retail flow was $3.8B versus a 12-month average of $6.4B/week. ETFs took +$4.0B and single stocks -$0.2B. NVDA +$1,596M accounted for most of the single-stock buying. Outside Mag 7, retail sold every sector, led by Industrials (-$514M), Financials (-$429M), Cons. Disc. (-$389M) and Health Care (-$381M).

Momentum crowding: Momentum (L/S) is down ~40% from its May 11 peak, the largest unwind since the post-GFC recovery. October was the worst month in ~40 years for long Momentum vs. market (-11%, ~6 sigma), and multiples de-rated ~4x from January highs. JPM calls it a deleveraging event, not a fundamental break in the AI cycle.

Capitulation indicators: Momentum crowding fell from the 100th to the 81st percentile of its 40-year history and stood at the 0th/5th/43rd percentile vs 1-, 3- and 5-year histories as of Nov 5. JPM's broad leverage index recorded its largest deleveraging since the 2022 post-COVID downturn, exceeding Liberation Day.

JPM sees an intra-cycle reset rather than end-cycle, which would involve large downward 2027 earnings revisions. It views the midterms as a clearing event and expects data center headwinds to be better than feared.

Electrical Equipment/Multi-Industry analysts say the AI capex up-cycle is in year 4 and maturing, with higher rates raising ROI hurdles. They expect AI-related EE/MI valuations to stay pressured but a sharp bounce after the sell-off is likely. They are Neutral on ETN, JCI and VRT and like GEV and TT for earnings visibility.

GOOGL expanded its 8th-gen TPU lineup. JPM analysts expect the v8i Max inference TPU to ramp ~2H27 and the 2nm v9.5/v10 TPU to enter production mid-2028. They see no gaps in Broadcom's TPU roadmap and no slowdown in AVGO revenue growth through CY31.

CRWV 3Q: operating margin 10%, a quarter ahead of plan, with 4Q26 guided to ~16%. Management plans to address the 2027 committed backlog with under $5B of parent-level equity or equity-linked raises and expects no unsecured debt raise in 2027. Retail took profits (-1.5z on 11/11).
COHR raised long-term guidance: 60%+ pro forma revenue growth in FY27, a first $3B revenue quarter in FY27 and a first $4B quarter in FY28. The stock is up 36% since the report.

APP is up 51% since reporting on 11/5 after upside in 3Q revenue and a solid 4Q outlook. The company began a partial rollout of next-gen Axon models and reiterated a 30%+ annualized revenue growth goal.

FIS is down ~27% since reporting. Banking recurring growth slowed almost 3ppts on bank conversion delays, and 2027 guidance was cut. JPM analysts say it will take multiple quarters of execution and positive revisions to rebuild confidence.
TTWO rose 7% on 11/10 ahead of the GTA VI console release. It reiterated FY27 bookings guidance of $8.0B-$8.2B (+19%-22%), and JPM analysts see upside to guidance from GTA VI unit sales.

Meme/high-short-interest names: SOC fell 54.4% on Nov 9 on a going-concern warning, then fell 14.7% more on Nov 10, and retail bought ~$30M across the two sessions. OPEN fell 21.8% on Nov 6 after a Q3 revenue miss and weak guidance. QNT rose 26% on Nov 6 after a Q3 beat and raised 2026 revenue outlook.

Retail options share is nearly at its 1-year low, though the rolling 1-month average of the model's share is at the 78.8th percentile. Most-traded options: NVDA, MU, TSLA, AMD, SNDK, META, AMZN, GOOG/L, AAPL, MSFT. Futures traders (non-retail) net sold ~$3.4B: NQ ~$5.1B and RTY ~$3.3B sold, ES ~$5.0B bought.

CDS-based stock screen (IG universe, composite of 67% contrarian and 33% confirmation signals): top-ranked names include CPB, CAG, ORCL, DXC, MSFT and AMD. Bottom-ranked include TEVA, DAL, RCL, CCL, ALLY and COF.

TTWO reiterated FY27 bookings guidance of $8.0B-$8.2B (+19%-22%) (company guidance, reiterated).

COHR reported: results and next-quarter guidance ahead of consensus. Long-term guidance: 60%+ pro forma FY27 revenue growth, a first $3B revenue quarter in FY27 and a first $4B quarter in FY28 (company targets). Scale-across/DCI revenue is expected to ramp to $400M+ per quarter by end of CY27.
APP 3Q reported: revenue growth upside and a solid 4Q growth outlook. The company reiterated a 30%+ annualized revenue growth goal.
FIS 3Q reported: headline results broadly ahead of expectations and at the high end of guidance. Banking recurring growth slowed almost 3ppts and 2027 guidance was cut.
OPEN 3Q reported: revenue of $1.02B missed estimates, the net loss widened and 4Q guidance fell short of consensus. The stock fell 21.8% on Nov 6.
QNT 3Q reported: revenue of $9.1M (+233% YoY) on record bookings of $98M. 2026 revenue outlook raised to $31-34M, above consensus.
